title: Add cross-process RMW lock for concurrent index writes
context: MCP server and CLI hooks write .hunch/ concurrently; two unsynchronized read-modify-writes over index.json silently erase the second writer's records (issue #35). Touches invariant(s): con_902759b3dc (All JSON writes to .hunch/ must be atomic (temp-file + rename) so an interrupted write can never truncate the index); con_947c578b2c (Forward-migrate raw JSON to the current schema BEFORE Zod validation; never silently drop unmigratable records); con_a87360128b (Semantic vectors are a derived layer in SQLite, never the source of truth; reconcile by content hash on reindex).
decision: Introduce mkdirSync-based cross-process mutex with bounded 2-second spin-wait and stale-lock takeover by age (10s TTL). Gracefully degrade to uncoordinated write with warning if lock is still held at deadline, rather than throwing.
consequences: Prevents silent record erasure under concurrent index modifications
Adds ~25ms latency per contending writer waiting for lock
Requires stale-lock detection and forcible reclamation when process dies while holding lock
Capture paths never fail due to lock contention—degrade to best-effort with warning instead
alternatives_rejected: Remain lockless: silent record loss under concurrency (reproduces the bug)
Strict indefinite-wait lock: deadlocks when a process dies while holding the lock
Lock that throws on contention: breaks mandatory capture operations that cannot fail
Filesystem-level coordination (atomic renames only): cannot atomically update both old and new records
